hints: Focus on what functional group is actually present at C1 and at C2, and recall what acidified dichromate can and cannot oxidise.
Notice that C1 is already a ketone $\text{C=O}$ so it cannot be oxidised further, while C2 is a secondary alcohol $\text{CH-OH}$ so only C2 can react.
Now check the molecular formula by counting carbons and hydrogens carefully, then count carbons joined to four different groups to test the last two statements.
walkthrough:
**Test Statement 1 - Oxidation with K2Cr2O7**

Acidified $\text{K}_2\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7$ is a strong oxidising agent for alcohols. Primary alcohols go to aldehydes then carboxylic acids, secondary alcohols go to ketones, but ketones and tertiary alcohols are not oxidised.

Rule:
$$\text{secondary alcohol} \xrightarrow{[O]} \text{ketone, ketone} \xrightarrow{[O]} \text{no reaction}$$

**Apply to C1 and C2**

C1 is the $\text{C=O}$ carbon in the six-membered ring. It is a ketone, already fully oxidised at that carbon, so no further oxidation.

C2 is the $\text{CH-OH}$ carbon in the five-membered ring. It is a secondary alcohol, so it can be oxidised to a ketone. Because only C2 and not C1 can be oxidised, statement 1 which claims both can be is false.

**Test Statement 2 - Count Hydrogen Atoms**

Testosterone has 4 fused rings with formula $\text{C}_{19}\text{H}_{28}\text{O}_2$. You can get this by counting all skeletal carbons (17 in the steroid skeleton plus 2 $\text{CH}_3$ groups = 19) and then adding hydrogens to give each carbon four bonds.

There are 28 hydrogens, which is not fewer than 27, so statement 2 is false.

**Test Statement 3 - Count Chiral Centres**

A chiral carbon is $sp^3$ carbon joined to four different groups. $\text{C=O}$ carbons, $\text{C=C}$ carbons and $\text{CH}_2$ carbons cannot be chiral.

In testosterone, six $sp^3$ ring-junction and side carbons each carry H plus three different ring fragments or methyl groups. That gives six chiral centres, so statement 3 is true.

**Combine the Conclusions**

Statement 1 is false, statement 2 is false, statement 3 is true. Only 3 is correct, which matches 3 only.

options.A: This claims 1 only is correct. Statement 1 is false because C1 is a ketone and ketones resist oxidation by acidified $\text{K}_2\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7$. Only the secondary alcohol at C2 is oxidised.
options.B: This claims 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 3 is correct with six chiral centres, but statement 2 is false. Testosterone is $\text{C}_{19}\text{H}_{28}\text{O}_2$ with 28 hydrogens, not fewer than 27.
options.C: This claims 2 only is correct. Statement 2 is false because careful counting gives 28 H atoms. Students often miss one H on the skeleton or miscount the $\text{CH}_3$ and $\text{CH}_2$ groups.
options.D: This claims 3 only is correct. Statement 1 is false (C1 ketone cannot be oxidised), statement 2 is false (28 H, not <27), and statement 3 is true (six carbons with four different substituents). Well done for checking each functional group carefully.
